pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: VSOCK: use TCP state constants for sk_state There are two state fields: socket->state and sock->sk_state. The socket->state field uses SS_UNCONNECTED, SS_CONNECTED, etc while the sock->sk_state typically uses values that match TCP state constants (TCP_CLOSE, TCP_ESTABLISHED). AF_VSOCK does not follow this convention and instead uses SS_* constants for both fields. The sk_state field will be exposed to userspace through the vsock_diag interface for ss(8), netstat(8), and other programs. This patch switches sk_state to TCP state constants so that the meaning of this field is consistent with other address families. Not just AF_INET and AF_INET6 use the TCP constants, AF_UNIX and others do too. The following mapping was used to convert the code: SS_FREE -> TCP_CLOSE SS_UNCONNECTED -> TCP_CLOSE SS_CONNECTING -> TCP_SYN_SENT SS_CONNECTED -> TCP_ESTABLISHED SS_DISCONNECTING -> TCP_CLOSING VSOCK_SS_LISTEN -> TCP_LISTEN In __vsock_create() the sk_state initialization was dropped because sock_init_data() already initializes sk_state to TCP_CLOSE. Signed-off-by: Stefan Hajnoczi <stefanha@redhat.com> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit 3b4477d2dcf2709d0be89e2a8dced3d0f4a017f2) Signed-off-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:848063 TEST=while true; do curl localhost:8080; done Conflicts: net/vmw_vsock/hyperv_transport.c - does not exist in 4.4 Cq-Depend: chromium:1717816 Change-Id: I5beab4d252fd81ee5c349f9067ce260cb2b6e0e6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1696746 Tested-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Verkamp <dverkamp@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: vsock/virtio: set SOCK_DONE on peer shutdown Set the SOCK_DONE flag to match the TCP_CLOSING state when a peer has shut down and there is nothing left to read. This fixes the following bug: 1) Peer sends SHUTDOWN(RDWR). 2) Socket enters TCP_CLOSING but SOCK_DONE is not set. 3) read() returns -ENOTCONN until close() is called, then returns 0. Signed-off-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit 42f5cda5eaf4396a939ae9bb43bb8d1d09c1b15c) BUG=chromium:848063 TEST=while true; do curl localhost:8080; done Change-Id: I8e03e006a17afeaee7720747d1771710c45ec58c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1696747 Tested-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Verkamp <dverkamp@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

cryptohome: remove SHA1 check in DecryptScrypt The SHA1 MAC here is redundant since scryptenc_buf already appends a MAC to the result buffer. Thus, the only way we could fail checking this extra hash without failing first in DecryptScryptBlob is if the hash itself was somehow tampered with or corrupted, which doesn't have any bearing on the integrity of the decrypted blob, so it can be safely ignored. BUG=chromium:984782 TEST=unit tests, deploy, attempt to mount vault using scrypt successfully and also with tampered vault keyset Change-Id: I5318a2454e43c6f2c103b3c2545a2589cd71efa0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1703936 Tested-by: Greg Kerr <kerrnel@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Greg Kerr <kerrnel@chromium.org>
